summary: Sarvam AI upgrades its 105B model with faster inference and lower operating costs

sentences: Bengaluru-based Sarvam AI has released an upgraded version of its 105-billion-parameter artificial intelligence model, introducing improvements in instruction following, tool calling and Indian language capabilities while reducing inference costs.
Named Sarvam-105B-1711, the updated model was announced on November 22 and is part of the company's Flash-Lite category.
The release strengthens Sarvam AI's focus on developing AI models and infrastructure suited to enterprise applications.

The company says the upgrade delivers better performance across several benchmarks, alongside faster processing and options for organisations that want to deploy AI systems within their own infrastructure.
The model achieved an average score of 73.9 across eight evaluations covering instruction following, conversational performance, tool calling and Indian languages.
These results are based on the company's own evaluations and are not an independent assessment of performance in real-world deployments.
Today we're releasing Sarvam-105B-1711, our new checkpoint of 105B model in the Flash-Lite category.

Averaged across instruction following, chat, tool calling and Indian languages, it sets a new Pareto frontier when compared with other popular Flash-Lite models. pic.twitter.com/mn1YP38EOg
Sarvam AI has introduced changes to the model's inference process using NVFP4 quantisation and a speculative decoding technique called DSpark.

According to the company, these optimisations enable the model to generate approximately 6,000 tokens per second on a single Nvidia B200 GPU when serving 64 concurrent users, around twice the speed of its earlier setup.
The company has also reported a significant reduction in inference costs.
Its blended inference price has fallen from $0.44 to $0.15 per million tokens, equivalent to approximately ₹13.75.
This blended rate combines input and output usage under a specified token mix and should not be interpreted as a flat price for one million output tokens.
Sarvam AI said the model was trained on its B200 GPU cluster.
The company also reported that its eight-bit pre-training approach increased model FLOPs utilisation from 19% to 38%.
Continued pre-training extended the context window to 160,000 tokens, enabling the model to process longer inputs.
A key feature of Sarvam-105B-1711 is the availability of a compressed version designed to run on a single Nvidia RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell workstation GPU with 96GB of memory.
The company has released its model weights in two formats.
The BF16 version is intended for fine-tuning and further training, while the compressed NVFP4 version supports inference and is approximately 65GB in size.
This deployment option could be relevant for enterprises that need greater control over sensitive information and prefer to run AI applications on their own premises.
Sarvam AI has highlighted potential use cases involving banks, government departments and other organisations with specific data-handling requirements.
The company has also connected the upgraded model with its Indus Cowork product and voice-agent applications.
Its Samvaad service uses a voice-specific fine-tuned version of the model rather than the standard checkpoint alone.
Sarvam AI said the updated model improves performance in Indian language tasks, instruction following and tool calling compared with its earlier version.
The company also reported improvements in its internal Indic language evaluation, although the results should be considered in the context of its testing methodology.
The model is designed to support AI agents that can follow instructions, interact with tools and handle business workflows.
These capabilities are increasingly relevant for customer support, enterprise automation and voice-based applications.
Sarvam AI has priced the model at ₹10 per million input tokens and ₹25 per million output tokens.
Its lower blended inference cost and workstation deployment option offer businesses different ways to evaluate and use the model, depending on their workloads and infrastructure requirements.
The release comes amid wider discussion around Sarvam AI's Token Factory initiative and its approach to building domestic AI infrastructure.

With Sarvam-105B-1711, the company is continuing to develop its model portfolio while focusing on inference efficiency, Indian language support and enterprise deployment flexibility.
